newsitem.title: GERMANY: SKW Trostberg-no need to up capital at the moment.
newsitem.headline: SKW Trostberg-no need to up capital at the moment.

text.p: German specialty chemicals company SKW Trostberg said on Wednesday that it did not plan any capital increase in the near future and said not to expect any spectacular takeovers in 1997.

"From an economic point of view there is no reason for a capital increase," Klaus-Juergen Shulz, Trostberg's chief financial officer, told journalists at a news conference to announce the group's nine-month results.
The reason for this was that terms for obtaining external capital were very reasonable at the moment, while equity capital would prove more expensive through a capital raise, said Schulz.
SKW would finance the 1.3 billion Swiss franc takeover of MBT from Sandoz in different currencies, including dollars, yen, deutschemarks and French francs.
Around 1.1 billion Swiss francs would be paid in cash, while the group would take over a total of 200 million francs of financial debt.
